title: Role Activation — Failure Mode Analysis and Recovery Playbook
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Summary

Purpose: This playbook documents the common failure modes that delay or block role activation (the state where a new hire has full access, assigned mentor, and first-week objectives) and prescribes step-by-step recovery actions, ownership, SLAs, and escalation paths. Use this doc when an activation milestone is missed or when recurring failure patterns are identified.

Scope
- Applies to all full-time, contractor, and intern hires across engineering, product, and GTM who require cross-functional provisioning (accounts, desk equipment, manager/mentor pairing).
- Excludes contractors on short-term task-only engagements that follow a separate light-onboarding checklist.

Expected outcomes
- Restore a blocked activation within defined SLAs.
- Capture root cause and action items to prevent recurrence.
- Update metric dashboards for Time-to-Activation and Activation Success Rate.

Key definitions
- Role Activation: New hire has (a) corporate account & required service accounts; (b) equipment assigned; (c) manager and mentor assigned; (d) Day-1 and Week-1 objectives visible in LMS/OKR tool.
- Activation Failure: Any event causing Role Activation to exceed 7 business days or miss required Day-1 deliverables.

Ownership and responsibilities
- People Ops (Onboarding Team): Primary owner for provisioning coordination, SLA tracking, and first escalation. (Contact: onboarding@redwood.com)
- IT/Cloud Access (Infra): Responsible for cloud accounts, VPN/VPC access, service accounts, MFA enforcement and device imaging.
- Hiring Manager: Responsible for mentor assignment, role-specific access approvals, and first-week objectives.
- Facilities/Hardware Ops: Device procurement and physical provisioning.
- Security: Clearances, privileged access approvals, and KBA where required.

Activation SLAs and metrics
(Goal: measure and enforce predictable activations)

SLA table
| Metric | Target | Escalation threshold | Owner | Notes |
|--------|--------|----------------------|-------|-------|
| Time-to-Activation (full) | <= 7 business days (95% of hires) | 5 business days | People Ops | Start timer at offer acceptance + signed I-9/equivalent where applicable |
| Account Provisioning (corporate) | <= 2 business days | 2 business days | IT/Cloud Access | Includes email, SSO, device enrollment |
| Cloud Service Access (role-specific) | <= 5 business days | 3 business days | IT/Cloud Access + Manager | Approvals often require manager action; track via access-request ticket |
| Equipment Delivery | <= 5 business days (US) | 3 business days | Facilities/Hardware Ops | International shipping windows vary; document exceptions |
| Mentor Assignment | <= 3 business days | 3 business days | Hiring Manager | If not assigned, People Ops assigns temporary buddy |

Operational metrics to report weekly
- Activation Success Rate (30d rolling)
- Median Time-to-Activation
- Number of incidents per cohort that triggered this playbook
- Top 3 recurring root causes

Common failure modes and recovery steps
1) Missing or delayed corporate account provisioning
- Symptoms: No SSO account, cannot access email or Slack, identity provider shows "pending".
- Immediate triage (first 30 minutes): People Ops confirms identity docs present in HRIS and that provisioning ticket exists. Capture ticket ID and timestamp.
- Recovery steps:
  a) People Ops opens priority ticket with IT/Cloud Access and tags "activation-critical".
  b) IT validates SSO config and forces provisioning; if tenant limit reached, IT notifies Cloud Access lead.
  c) If device-dependent (device not imaged) provide temporary web-based workstation and escalate device shipment.
- Owner: IT/Cloud Access (primary), People Ops (coordinator)
- Post-mortem: Update provisioning checklist and track whether a human approval step was the blocker.

2) Manager/mentor not assigned or unavailable
- Symptoms: New hire has no scheduled check-in, no day-1 objectives.
- Immediate triage: People Ops pings hiring manager; if no response in 4 business hours, People Ops assigns an interim buddy from the team schedule.
- Recovery steps:
  a) People Ops uses 'Manager Escalation Matrix' to reach manager's backup.
  b) Assign interim mentor and schedule day-1 intro.
  c) Notify manager that failure to assign repeatedly will trigger manager coaching and a note in performance calibration.
- Owner: Hiring Manager (primary), People Ops (escalation executor)

3) Privileged/cloud access approval stalled by security review
- Symptoms: Access ticket in "awaiting security review" for >48 hours.
- Immediate triage: People Ops/IT opens a policy exception request or temporary least-privilege access with an expiration (48–72 hours).
- Recovery steps:
  a) Security toggles temporary access with strict monitoring and requirement to submit required docs within 72 hours.
  b) People Ops schedules a compliance check and documents the exception with justification.
- Owner: Security (approver), IT (implementation), People Ops (documentation)

4) Hardware or shipping delays (international hires)
- Symptoms: Device delivery delayed beyond expected window, customs hold, or lost shipment.
- Immediate triage: Facilities confirms carrier status and triggers RMA/expedite.
- Recovery steps:
  a) Offer loaner device or secure desktop access.
  b) For long delays (>10 business days) issue stipend and document cost center.
- Owner: Facilities/Hardware Ops

5) Mismatch between role expectation and job setup (wrong groups/permissions)
- Symptoms: User has access but key services missing (e.g., repo access, dataset access).
- Immediate triage: Hiring Manager and People Ops audit role checklist; create list of missing items.
- Recovery steps:
  a) Submit role-specific access ticket with clear list and justification.
  b) Cross-team owner meeting within 48 hours to resolve entitlement mapping.
- Owner: Hiring Manager (requester), IT (entitlements), Product/Platform (resource owners)

Escalation matrix
- Level 1 (Operational): People Ops onboarding lead — onboarding@redwood.com — response SLA 4 business hours.
- Level 2 (Team lead): IT Cloud Access lead / Facilities lead / Security lead — response SLA 8 business hours.
- Level 3 (Director): Director, People Ops and Director, IT — response SLA 24 business hours; engage exec on-call for customer-impacting delays.

Runbook: Immediate 8-step triage (use when an activation misses an SLA threshold)
1) Record the hire and what was missed in the Activation Tracker (spreadsheet/ticket).
2) Capture ticket IDs for every affected system and assign severity=high.
3) Contact hiring manager and confirm critical services required day-1.
4) Assign an interim buddy if mentor is not available.
5) Create temporary access if security allows least-privilege exceptions.
6) Expedite device shipping or provision cloud workstation.
7) Communicate status to hire with expected timeline and single point of contact.
8) Trigger post-mortem if activation > 7 business days or if a recurring failure pattern emerges.

Templates and artifacts (copy into HRIS / onboarding ticket)
- Activation ticket template (subject): [Activation-Critical] New Hire: <Name> — Missing: <items> — TicketIDs: <list>
- Communication template (to new hire):
  Hi <Name>, we are working on the remaining items needed for your activation. Current ETA: <date>. Your onboarding lead is <Name> (<email>). We will provide temporary access where possible.

Post-mortem and continuous improvement
- Trigger conditions: activation > 7 business days OR identical failure mode for 3 hires in 30 days.
- Post-mortem steps:
  1) People Ops creates incident doc with timeline, owners, root cause, and action items.
  2) Assign owners to remediate systemic issues (e.g., add automation, update runbooks, change SLAs).
  3) Track remediation to closure in the 'Activation Reliability' board and report monthly to People Ops leadership.

Preventative actions and long-term mitigations
- Automate provisioning for repeatable role templates (engineer, data scientist, sales) using Terraform or IAM automation.
- Maintain a pool of loaner devices and pre-imaged images for cross-region hires.
- Quarterly access entitlement audits to identify misconfigured role templates.
- Manager readiness checklist and automated reminders 5 business days before start date to ensure mentor assignment and project setup.

Tooling and dashboards
- Activation Tracker (Google Sheet) — primary ledger for SLA calculation.
- Onboarding tickets: our Jira project ONB- (labels: activation-critical).
- Weekly report: Activation Metrics dashboard in Looker / internal observability.

Related policies and links
- Hiring policy for international shipments: /people-ops/shipping-policy-2025
- SSO and IAM policy: /security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/iam-policy-2024
- Manager onboarding expectations: /people-ops/manager-accelerated-integration-framework-2025

Appendix: Quick checklists
- Pre-start (5 business days before): Offer accepted, signed docs, manager invited to schedule intro, device requested, initial role access template selected.
- Day 0/1: Account, Slack, email, meeting with manager, mentor intro, 1st week objectives visible.
- Day 7: Confirm access to role-specific systems and first week progress check.
- Day 30: Role baseline established and initial feedback collected.

Document maintenance
- Owner: People Ops Onboarding (Priya Kapoor). Review cadence: quarterly or after any activation post-mortem.

Notes
- This playbook complements our existing onboarding templates; use it for incidents and systemic reliability improvements.
- If a legal or customer-sensitive issue is implicated, mark the incident confidential and escalate to Security and Legal immediately.
